about.title: Rule race: molding-press
about.method: Every rule ran 40 times on the same customer orders, each run 60 days long. Rules with settings to try were tuned first on 30 practice runs with other orders. Ranges are 95% ranges of the average, paired run by run.

recommendation.label: Family campaign
recommendation.sentence: Run Family campaign instead of Lowest cover. It makes $22,088 more per run, about $134,370 more a year.
recommendation.why: Main reason: it spends $35,355 less per run on changeovers. It has 33 fewer changeovers to another family.

delta.assumption: A year is 365 days, so about 6.1 runs of 60 days. Each run starts fresh, so this is a rough guide.

long_check.words: A 180-day check gives about $109,000 more a year.

confidence.detail: We are 95% sure it earns between $19,733 and $24,444 more per run on average. It came out ahead in 40 of 40 runs.

floor.label: Changeovers per run
floor.note: Colour changes drop from 41 to 8. Those cost $1,200 each.

floor.label: Orders filled from stock
floor.note: Fewer orders find an empty shelf.

floor.label: Stock on hand
floor.note: You need the room and the cash for it.

floor.label: Days the press rests
floor.note: Free time for upkeep. Part of it is the test ending at day 60.

floor.label: Sales lost per run
floor.note: That is $1,622 less in lost sales per run.

drivers.words: it spends $35,355 less per run on changeovers
it spends $1,622 less per run on lost sales

policies.label: Family campaign
policies.about: Stay with one family until it is stocked up, then move on.

policies.label: Reorder point
policies.about: The (s, S) rule: refill a product when it drops to s, up to S.

policies.label: Changeover-aware run-out
policies.about: Make what runs out first, but count a product switch as lost days.

policies.label: Kanban
policies.about: Kanban cards: refill a product when it drops under a share of its target.

policies.label: Lowest cover
policies.about: Make the product that will run out first.

policies.label: Lowest stock first
policies.about: Make the product that will run out first.

policies.label: ABC wheel
policies.about: Run products in a set order. Fast sellers get a turn often, slow sellers less often.

policies.label: Biggest dollar shortfall
policies.about: Run the product whose missing stock is worth the most money.

policies.label: Fixed wheel
policies.about: Run every product in the same order, a set number of days each.

policies.label: Best for today only
policies.about: Run what earns the most money today. It does not plan for tomorrow.

policies.label: Random
policies.about: Pick any product, or rest the press, at random.

tuning.words: Days per slot 2 gave the most profit. Days per slot 6 gave the least, $30,646 less per run. This rule is touchy. Check its setting again when demand changes.
Target days 8 gave the most profit. Target days 28 gave the least, $16,215 less per run. This rule is touchy. Check its setting again when demand changes.
Target days 16 gave the most profit. Target days 20 gave the least, $6,479 less per run. The settings were close, so a wrong pick costs little.
Days per slot 3 gave the most profit. Days per slot 6 gave the least, $23,891 less per run. This rule is touchy. Check its setting again when demand changes.
Target days 14, trigger share 0.7 gave the most profit. Target days 6, trigger share 0.5 gave the least, $5,036 less per run. The settings were close, so a wrong pick costs little.
Stop days 10 gave the most profit. Stop days 4 gave the least, $3,220 less per run. The settings were close, so a wrong pick costs little.
Stop days 10 gave the most profit. Stop days 6 gave the least, $2,184 less per run. The settings were close, so a wrong pick costs little.
Safety days 10, eoq scale 0.5 gave the most profit. Safety days 10, eoq scale 1 gave the least, $5,877 less per run. The settings were close, so a wrong pick costs little.

Cross penalty days 0.5, within penalty days 0 gave the most profit. Cross penalty days 0.5, within penalty days 2 gave the least, $39,128 less per run. This rule is touchy. Check its setting again when demand changes.

cautions.title: The gain comes late
cautions.body: It is behind today's rule until day 54 of 60. Test a longer run before you commit. A 180-day check gives about $109,000 more a year.

cautions.title: You will hold 2.6 times more stock
cautions.body: About 3,400 units on the shelf, up from 1,300. Check the room and the cash first.

cautions.title: Natural products still run short
cautions.body: Each natural product is out about 1 day in 6. With today's rule it is about 1 day in 7.
